origin_and_geography.native_tract: Tumkur, Hassan, Mysore, Mandya, Bangalore, and Chitradurga districts of Southern Karnataka, India.
origin_and_geography.agro_climatic_zone: Southern Deccan plateau, semi-arid scrub and dry tropical agricultural zone.
origin_and_geography.historical_background: One of the most illustrious draught breeds in Indian history. Maintained by the traditional Hallikar community and patronage of Mysore royal dynasty (Wodeyars). Progenitor of famous draught breeds including Amritmahal.

morphological_traits.horns: Long, vertical, sweeping backward and upward in an elegant curvature with sharp tapered tips bending inward.
morphological_traits.forehead: Narrow, prominent, with a slight furrow down the center.
morphological_traits.coat_color: Grey to dark iron-grey in bulls (especially over neck and shoulders); cows are generally light silver-grey.
morphological_traits.hump_and_dewlap: Well-developed, compact hump in males; tight, thin dewlap that does not hang loosely.
morphological_traits.body_conformation: Slender, deep-chested, muscular frame; high ground clearance, lean limbs, and extremely hard, small hooves.

production_and_utility.primary_utility: Heavy draught, fast agricultural tillage, and long-distance road carting.
production_and_utility.draught_capacity: Supreme endurance and trotting speed; able to haul heavy plows in dry hard-caked soils for 8-10 hours continuously.

management_and_resilience.diet_and_forage: Thrives on finger millet (ragi) straw, sorghum fodder, and local grazing commons.
management_and_resilience.disease_resistance: Outstanding resistance to tropical foot rot, heat stress, and piroplasmosis.
management_and_resilience.temperament: Spirited, energetic, courageous; highly responsive to skilled bullock cart drivers.

conservation_status: Conserved under Karnataka State Livestock Breeders Association and National Bureau of Animal Genetic Resources.
